judge.voice: Fine, B2 and not C1. I can live with that, and it quoted my own sentences, so I could not argue. The tasks were real meeting situations, not baby topics, which I liked. But I told it "we was discussing about" and "since 2010" in the first minutes, and "he don't agree" too. None of that came back. Those are exactly what the new US director hears. It fixed "plan how we fix it" and "customer trust", which is useful but not the main problem. It also praised my meeting answer for "accurate grammar" when I know I made slips. That makes me trust the praise less. Seven minutes is acceptable. I would try it again if the practice goes after my real recurring errors. Right now it is a decent level check, not yet a fix.

Hello Dana. The 21st is too late for us, because our production line is waiting for this parts since Monday and we was planning to start the assembly on 17th. If we don't receive it before 18th, we will have a big delay and our customer will be not happy. Can you do a partial delivery earlier?
That makes sense, a stopped line is expensive. We might be able to send part of the order by the 18th. Which parts are most urgent for your line?

The most urgent are the brackets and the control units, because without them we can not start the assembly. The other parts we can wait until 21st, this is not a problem for us. If you send these two by 18th, I think we can find a solution together.
That helps a lot, Martin. So the brackets and control units by the 18th, and the rest by the 21st. I'll check that with the warehouse. How do you want to handle the timing from here?

Yes, this is good. Please confirm me by email today that the brackets and control units will be delivered by 18th, and I will inform my production team. If there is any problem in the warehouse, you must call me immediately, because we can not lose more time. Thank you for your help, Dana.
Agreed, Martin: brackets and control units by the 18th, the rest by the 21st. I'll email the confirmation today and call you straight away if the warehouse has a problem. Who should I copy?

judge.voice: The negotiation with Dana was exactly my job, and she spoke like a real supplier. Good. The "we was" catch was right and quick. But then I asked why it was wrong and got the same rule back, no real answer. And that's all? I said "confirm me" and "this parts" and nobody blinked, yet those are what the new director hears. Then the recap says B2 and doesn't say why. Nothing I can show my colleagues. I'd use it again for the scene, but I don't trust the level yet. It saves a little time over my language school, only if it learns to point at my repeated mistakes. Not worth a recommendation yet.
